authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Corteva completed its previously announced separation into two independent, publicly traded companies, spinning off its seed operating segment as Vylor Inc. (NYSE: VYLR) via a pro rata distribution to Corteva common stockholders.
Fifteen states and one sovereign commenced litigation in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana challenging the Corteva–Vylor separation and seeking injunctive relief.

The District Court issued a temporary restraining order enjoining Corteva and EIDP from disposing of assets outside the ordinary course and from paying dividends or repurchasing shares, absent a court order.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P10 (8-K Item 1.01/2.01).
business_model.claim: Corteva operated through two reporting segments, Seed and Crop Protection, before completing its separation into two independent companies on October 1, 2026.
quotes: The company's operations are managed through two operating segments: Seed and Crop Protection.

Corteva, Inc. (the "Company") completed its previously announced separation into two independent, publicly traded companies through the separation ("Separation") of the Company's seed operating segment into an independent, publicly traded company, Vylor Inc. ("Vylor").

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1, Business – Seed).
business_model.claim: The Seed segment develops and supplies commercial seed combining germplasm with advanced biotechnology traits to farmers in key markets including North America, Europe, Brazil, India, South Africa and Argentina.
quotes: The Seed segment develops and supplies commercial seed combining superior germplasm with advanced traits to produce high yield potential for farmers around the world.
The company's Seed segment is a leader in many key seed markets, including North America corn and soybeans, Europe corn and sunflower, as well as Brazil, India, South Africa and Argentina corn.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P6 (8-K earnings release segment tables).
business_model.claim: The Crop Protection segment sells herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, nitrogen stabilizers, biologicals and seed treatments to protect crops against weeds, insects, disease and to support crop health.
quotes: The Crop Protection segment serves the global agricultural input industry with products that protect against weeds, insects and other pests, and disease, and that support overall crop health both above and below ground via nitrogen management and seed-applied technologies.
Crop Protection net sales were approximately $3.73 billion for the first half of 2026 compared to approximately $3.63 billion in the same period of 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P3 (10-K Item 7, geographic sales table).
business_model.claim: Corteva's portfolio serves farmers in approximately 110 countries, with 2025 net sales of $17,401 million (table in millions) split roughly 52% North America, 22% Latin America, 18% EMEA and 8% Asia Pacific.
quotes: The company's broad portfolio of agriculture solutions fuels farmer productivity in approximately 110 countries.
The company reported net sales of $17,401 million, an increase of 3 percent versus the year ended December 31, 2024
North America | 9,024 | 52%

business_model.claim: Seed is distributed through four differentiated channels: the Pioneer agency model (direct farmer sales via independent representatives), regional seed brands, full-service retail storefronts, and third-party licensing and distribution.
quotes: The Seed segment has a diverse worldwide network which markets and distributes the company's brands to customers, primarily through the company's multi-channel, multi-brand strategy, which includes four differentiated channels: Pioneer agency model, regional seed brands, retail, as well as third parties through licensing and distribution channels.

business_model.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K Item 7) and P4 (10-Q Item 2 MD&A).
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by three primary levers—price, volume and currency—with 2025 full-year growth of 3% reflecting 1% price increase and 3% volume increase partially offset by 1% unfavorable currency.
quotes: The increase was primarily driven by a 1 percent increase in price and a 3 percent increase in volume, partially offset by a 1 percent unfavorable currency impact.

The company reported net sales of $6,379 million, down 1 percent versus the same quarter last year, reflecting a 3 percent decrease in volume, partially offset by a 1 percent increase in price and a 1 percent favorable impact from currency.

business_model.claim: Sales are seasonal, with approximately 60% of annual revenue generated in the first half of the calendar year aligned to northern-hemisphere planting, and accounts receivable peaks in H1 with cash collection concentrated in Q4.
quotes: The company typically generates about 60 percent of its sales in the first half of the calendar year, driven by northern hemisphere Seed and Crop Protection sales.
Accounts receivable tends to be higher during the first half of the year, consistent with the peak sales period in the northern hemisphere, with cash collection focused in the fourth quarter.

business_model.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K Item 7, COGS discussion) and P2 (10-K Item 1A, input cost risk).
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold is driven by raw material and commodity prices, net royalty expense, and productivity actions; 2025 COGS of $9,172 million (table in millions) represented 53% of net sales, down from 56% in 2024.
quotes: COGS was $9,172 million (53 percent of net sales) for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $9,529 million (56 percent of net sales) for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Corteva's input costs are variable based on the costs associated with production or with raw materials Corteva uses.

business_model.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K Item 7, R&D discussion) and P2 (10-K Item 1A, pipeline risk).
business_model.claim: R&D spending of $1,474 million (table in millions) in 2025 (8% of net sales) supports the breeding and biotechnology pipeline, with increases driven by higher employee compensation, contractor, consulting, field, lab and facilities costs.
quotes: R&D expense was $1,474 million (8 percent of net sales) for the year ended December 31, 2025 and $1,402 million (8 percent of net sales) for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The increase in R&D expense is in support of the company's long-term growth plans and was primarily driven by higher employee compensation costs due to variable compensation increases, as well as higher contractor, consulting and field, lab and facilities costs.

business_model.basis: Stated in P6 (8-K earnings release, Seed and Crop Protection summaries) and P4 (10-Q MD&A).
business_model.claim: Seed pricing and mix improvement is driven by demand for top technology and increased out-licensing income, while Crop Protection pricing faces competitive pressure, particularly in Latin America.
quotes: The increase in price/mix is due primarily to demand for top technology and increased out-licensing income.
Price declined 3% primarily due to the market dynamics in Latin America.

business_model.claim: Operating EBITDA was $3,848 million (table in millions) for full-year 2025, up from $3,376 million in 2024, driven by volume growth, favorable Seed price and mix, cost and productivity benefits and net royalty improvement.
quotes: Operating EBITDA was $3,848 million, up from $3,376 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily driven by volume growth, favorable Seed price and product mix, ongoing cost and productivity benefits and net royalty improvement, partially offset by continued investment in research and development, additional commissions and compensation expense, competitive Crop Protection pricing and unfavorable currency effects.

business_model.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K Item 7, Restructuring discussion) and P4 (10-Q MD&A, Recent Developments).
business_model.claim: The Crop Protection Operations Strategy Restructuring Program, approved November 2023, targets $650–$700 million in aggregate pre-tax charges and $180 million in run-rate savings by 2027, including exit of the Pittsburg, California site and cessation of production in Asturias, Spain.
quotes: The company expects to record aggregate pre-tax restructuring and asset related charges of $650 million to $700 million, comprised of $85 million to $105 million of severance and related benefit costs, $320 million to $340 million of asset-related and impairment charges, and $245 million to $255 million of costs related to exiting the company's production activities and ceasing operations

The Crop Protection Operations Strategy Restructuring Program is expected to contribute to the company's ongoing cost and productivity improvement efforts through achieving an estimated $180 million of savings on a run rate basis by 2027.

On June 12, 2026, the company disclosed that its management recently committed to the next phase of the plan to include the intended cessation of the company's production activities at its site in Asturias, Spain.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1, Crop Protection) and P10 (8-K Item 1.01/2.01).
business_model.claim: Following the October 1, 2026 separation, Corteva is a standalone Crop Protection company that plans to grow through differentiated sustainable product offerings including biologicals, with a focus on operational excellence and disciplined M&A.
quotes: As a separate company, the Crop Protection business plans to grow through its differentiated, sustainable product offerings, including biologicals, with a focus on operational excellence and disciplined mergers and acquisitions.
Vylor common stock commenced regular-way trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "VYLR" on October 1, 2026.

business_model.claim: On October 1, 2026, 15 states and one sovereign filed litigation challenging the Corteva–Vylor separation; a temporary restraining order was issued on October 9 but stayed on October 10 pending an emergency motion in the Seventh Circuit, and the separation was completed on October 1, 2026.
quotes: On October 1, 2026, 15 states and one sovereign commenced litigation in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana (the "District Court") challenging the separation of Corteva, Inc. ("Corteva" or the "Company") and Vylor Inc. ("Vylor") into two independent, publicly traded companies (the "Separation") and seeking injunctive relief in connection therewith.
The Order does not affect the completion of the Separation, which occurred on October 1, 2026, and the Order is not in effect pending resolution of the Motion.

competitive_position.claim: Corteva completed its separation into two independent publicly traded companies on October 1, 2026: Vylor (Seed) and New Corteva (Crop Protection), with Vylor common stock trading on the NYSE under the symbol VYLR.

competitive_position.claim: On October 1, 2026, 15 states and one sovereign filed litigation in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana challenging the Corteva-Vylor separation, and on October 9, 2026 the court issued a temporary restraining order enjoining asset disposals and dividend/share repurchase payments.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as a risk factor in the 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Corteva faces significant competition, and upon loss or expiration of patent protection for its products, it can lose a major portion of revenues for that product, which can have a material adverse effect on its business.
quotes: Corteva currently faces significant competition in the markets in which it operates.

Upon the loss or expiration of patent protection for one of Corteva's products or of a product that Corteva licenses, or upon the "at-risk" launch (despite pending patent infringement litigation against the generic product) by a generic manufacturer of a generic version of one of Corteva's patented products or of a product that Corteva licenses, Corteva can lose a major portion of revenues for that product, which can have a material adverse effect on Corteva's business.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as a risk factor in the 10-K Item 1A.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P7 (8-K filed 2026-10-14); the litigation, TRO, stay, and appeal are all described as factual events.
risks.claim: Fifteen states and one sovereign filed suit challenging the Corteva–Vylor separation, and a temporary restraining order was issued enjoining asset disposals, dividends, and share repurchases, though the order was stayed pending appeal.
quotes: On October 1, 2026, 15 states and one sovereign commenced litigation in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana (the "District Court") challenging the separation of Corteva, Inc. ("Corteva" or the "Company") and Vylor Inc. ("Vylor") into two independent, publicly traded companies (the "Separation") and seeking injunctive relief in connection therewith.
The Order enjoins each company from paying dividends or repurchasing shares of its common stock.

On October 10, 2026, at the request of the Company, Corteva and EIDP, the District Court stayed the Order pending resolution of an anticipated emergency motion (the "Motion") in the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit for a stay of the Order pending appeal.
The Order does not affect the completion of the Separation, which occurred on October 1, 2026, and the Order is not in effect pending resolution of the Motion.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K MD&A), P4 (10-Q MD&A), and F2 (10-Q income statement showing Business Separation Costs line item). All figures are directly quoted from the filings.
risks.claim: Corteva is executing two concurrent restructuring programs—the Crop Protection Operations Strategy Restructuring Program (total expected charges of $650 million to $700 million, with $611 million recorded through 2025) and the 2026 Restructuring Actions (estimated $115 million to $125 million of savings by 2027)—while also bearing $131 (table in millions) of business separation costs in H1 2026.
quotes: The company expects to record aggregate pre-tax restructuring and asset related charges of $650 million to $700 million, comprised of $85 million to $105 million of severance and related benefit costs, $320 million to $340 million of asset-related and impairment charges, and $245 million to $255 million of costs related to exiting the company's production activities and ceasing operations

Through the year ended December 31, 2025, the company recorded net pre-tax restructuring and asset related charges of $611 million inception-to-date under the Crop Protection Operations Strategy Restructuring Program

The 2026 Restructuring Actions are expected to contribute to the company's ongoing cost and productivity improvement efforts through achieving an estimated $115 million to $125 million of savings on a run rate basis by 2027.

risks.basis: Stated as a risk factor in P2 (10-K Item 1A). The specific mention of PFAS and EIDP legacy liabilities is stated; the magnitude of potential unmet liabilities is not quantified in the evidence.
risks.claim: Corteva is exposed to substantial environmental and legacy EIDP liabilities, including PFAS-related costs and soil/groundwater contamination, which the company acknowledges could be 'materially higher than Corteva's accruals.'
quotes: Environmental and health and safety laws, regulations and standards, including those with respect to PFAS and other substances, expose Corteva to the risk of substantial costs and liabilities, including liabilities associated with Corteva's business and the discontinued and divested businesses and operations of EIDP.
Accordingly, environmental, health or safety regulatory matters could result in significant unanticipated costs or liabilities, which may be materially higher than Corteva's accruals.
